title: Non-invasive Sublingual Glycocalyx Measurements Using GlycoCheck
author: Tracey L Weissgerber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be5ejg3e
materials: Wait for database synchronization to complete
On the calibration screen, select “Camera KK”
Wait until participant places camera under tongue
Select the trial that you want to export
Wipe the camera handle with a disinfecting wipe.
Message “Error Ocurred Scheduler Service is not running”

steps.title: Hardware Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare the computer and camera hardware for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Take out the computer and camera.
Plug the camera into a USB port on the right-hand side of the computer.
Turn on the computer.
Wait until the 'Process Scheduler' status on the taskbar shows as 'Idle'.
Plug the Hard Disk Drive into a USB port on the right-hand side of the computer.
Place a paper towel in front of the computer to manage drooling.

steps.title: Prepare Camera Probe
steps.instruction: Prepare the camera probe with a new cover while the computer boots.

substeps.instruction: Remove the storage probe cover and place it in the camera spot of the suitcase.
Open the packaging for a new probe cover.
Gently place the new probe cover on the camera, leaving it in the packaging.

steps.title: Software Initialization and Patient Entry
steps.instruction: Launch the GlycoCheck software and register the participant.

substeps.instruction: Open the Glycocheck-New program.
Click 'Start Calibration'.
Select 'Add new patient' from the drop-down menu and enter: Patient ID, test date (in birthday field), first 3 letters of last name, first 3 letters of first name, and gender.
Click 'Add patient' to add the patient to the database.
Click 'Admission' to ensure the patient appears in the list on the right.
Click the battery charging signal in the lower right corner and ensure 'High Performance' is selected.
Verify that the correct participant is selected in the 'Admissions' List.

steps.title: Participant Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the participant for the sublingual measurement.

substeps.instruction: Ask the participant to swallow to clear saliva and reduce air bubbles.
Show the participant a picture of blood vessels underneath the tongue, targeting big vessels at the back, just right or left of center.
Demonstrate how to hold the camera with two hands wrapped around the base and forearms/arms supported on the desk.
Inform the participant that you will focus the camera using the black knob and provide instructions throughout the protocol.

Instruct the participant to raise their tongue slightly and place the camera under the tongue, just touching the surface without applying pressure (do this before turning on the camera to avoid discomfort from the bright green flashing LED light).
Press 'Perform selected visit'.
Focus the camera once a stable image is found; continue focusing throughout the test as needed without moving the camera.
If a crystalline structure is visible, the camera is focused on the plastic cover; turn the black knob until vessels and flowing red blood cells are in focus.
If the camera is very out of focus while the green bar is increasing, stop the trial and start over; do not use that data.

Collect several videos of different vessels from slightly different locations: once the green bar increases by 1/5 to 1/6, ask the participant to move the camera slightly to find new vessels, then hold stable for recording.
If only small looping vessels are seen, encourage the participant to move the camera toward the back and center of the tongue.
Remind the participant to breathe through their nose.
If an air bubble is present or the red warning light is on, ask the participant to move the camera slightly until the bubble is gone.
If cells are not flowing or flow is slow/changing, ensure the camera is gently touching the tongue without pressing into it.
If the 5:00 timer runs out, click 'continue' and note the extra time in the trial comments.
If the participant needs a break, press 'Abort'; press 'Cancel' to resume.

steps.title: Post-Trial Processing
steps.instruction: Complete the trial and record metadata.

substeps.instruction: Once the program stops automatically, remove the camera and place the probe cover back in the protective sleeve.

In the comments field, record: time of day, fasting status (and time of last meal if not fasted), caffeine intake in the prior 6 hours, if extra time was needed, reasons why data should not be used, and other factors (stress, smoking, medications, position).
Click 'Next patient'.
Wait 30 seconds for calculations to start (or click 'perform new visit' before 30 seconds to do two trials back-to-back).
Go to 'Patient Screen' (this may take a minute to appear for the first trial).
Wait 5 minutes for calculations to complete. Do not unplug, shut down, remove the camera, or start a new trial during this time.

steps.title: Trial Repetition and Data Export
steps.instruction: Repeat the process for multiple trials and export the results.

substeps.instruction: Perform a total of 3 trials per participant by repeating the collection and processing steps.
Go to 'Measurement Screen' and click 'Export Data'.
Adjust the filename by adding T1, T2, or T3 to correspond with the trial number.
Repeat the export process until all trials are saved.

steps.title: System Shutdown and Storage
steps.instruction: Safely power down and store the equipment.

substeps.instruction: Close the Glycocheck program only after all calculations are complete.
Remove and discard the used probe cover and replace the storage probe cover.
Place the camera in the box, coiling the cord into the designated space.
Ensure the computer battery is fully charged and place the battery in the lower part of the suitcase.
Place the computer in the suitcase with the tongue picture and patient schedule on top.
Ensure the camera cord is not sticking out to prevent damage when closing the suitcase.

steps.title: Troubleshooting
steps.instruction: Address software errors or hardware contamination.

substeps.instruction: If the program fails to start or complete: restart the computer, right-click 'Process scheduler' and select 'Start Service'. If that fails, check 'gmt-pss' in the Task Manager 'Services' tab and start it. If both fail, email GlycoCheck.
If the 'License is expired' message appears, contact GlycoCheck for an update.

If dark specks (dust) appear on the image: remove the protective cover and the camera extension, replace the camera and put on a new lens cover, then use a long-handled lint-free cotton swab to gently rub the lens. Run a test to verify cleanliness before replacing the protective lens cover.
